provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Mech family batch. Licensed and agency-saturated, so copy leans on owner-run, answered-phone contrast. No equipment brands, no rebate or tax-credit amounts, no response-time promises. Ranges are planning figures.

pageStructurePlus.section: Repair or replace your furnace or AC
pageStructurePlus.contains: Age of the furnace or air conditioner, repeat breakdowns, refrigerant type on older condensers, uneven rooms, rising utility bills, and when one more repair is the honest call
pageStructurePlus.why: Every no-heat or no-cool call ends with 'should I just replace it'. A straight answer before the visit makes the technician the adviser, not the salesman.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How a heat pump heats in a cold snap, backup heat strips, dual-fuel with a gas furnace, and bracketed placeholders for any utility rebate the owner confirms
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners hear about heat pumps from neighbours and the news. The contractor who explains them plainly gets the replacement quote.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Why a bigger unit short-cycles, a room-by-room load calculation, duct size checks, the hot upstairs bedroom, and what the visit measures
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers compare quotes by tonnage and price. Explaining sizing shows why a cheaper oversized system costs more to live with.

pageStructurePlus.section: HVAC install day, step by step
pageStructurePlus.contains: Old equipment removal, attic or crawlspace access, line set and pad, permit and city inspection, thermostat setup, startup readings, and the walkthrough
pageStructurePlus.why: A full changeout means a crew in the house for a day. Knowing exactly what happens removes the last reason to put the install off.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Leaky ducts, dusty rooms, filter sizes and change intervals, whole-home humidifiers and dehumidifiers, and air cleaners, described without health claims
pageStructurePlus.why: Comfort complaints that aren't the equipment are usually the ducts. This page turns a tune-up call into a duct or humidity job.

designDirections.name: Service Ticket
designDirections.bestFor: One- and two-van HVAC shops that live on repair calls and want the phone and the service form doing all the work
designDirections.headlineSample: Furnace and AC repair in {City}, from the owner's own van
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a neutral grotesque read like a clean service ticket. Nothing on the page competes with the call button.

designDirections.name: Redline Dispatch
designDirections.bestFor: Established heating and cooling companies that take no-heat and no-cool calls after hours and sell a maintenance plan
designDirections.headlineSample: No heat or no AC in {City}? Call the HVAC team that answers
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. A red call button on white with mono labels for hours and diagnostic fees says 'open now' faster than any photo of a smiling tech.

designDirections.name: Quiet Comfort
designDirections.bestFor: Replacement-led contractors selling heat pumps, zoning and whole-home air quality to larger and older homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Whole-home comfort systems, designed room by room in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy, brass and an editorial serif slow the reader down for a once-in-fifteen-years purchase where the design of the system matters more than speed.

openers.line: Your Google listing has Call and Directions but no website, so someone with a dead furnace can't check your HVAC hours or service area before deciding who to ring.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button for an HVAC shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook. Someone pricing a new air conditioner wants your maintenance plan and a service form, not a feed of truck posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest install they posted there.
openers.linkLine: A page built for the furnace and AC buyer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The HVAC site on your listing still shows a free-host banner and an old copyright year. People buying a system that lasts fifteen years want to know the installer will be around for the warranty call.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a dead contact form. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: Same heating and cooling company, current and quick on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your HVAC site on my phone and the call button was hidden behind the menu. Most no-heat searches happen on a phone in a cold kitchen.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks: menu, call button or form. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your HVAC site rebuilt for a phone in a cold house: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to book a furnace tune-up or report a noisy condenser except calling. A lot of people would rather type the problem at night than leave a voicemail.
openers.hook: Check the listing, the social pages and any site for a form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A service request that asks what the system is doing: {demo-link}

openers.line: You mention a maintenance plan in a post, but there's nowhere to sign up for it. A spring AC check and an autumn furnace check is the easiest recurring money in HVAC.
openers.hook: Look for any mention of a club, agreement or tune-up plan in posts or reviews. Quote the wording they use.
openers.linkLine: Your HVAC maintenance plan with a sign-up button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a tech who came out the same night the furnace quit and explained everything. Nobody reads that unless they're already on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one specific phrase about a heating or cooling repair. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those HVAC reviews next to the services they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first heat wave in {City} is when every air conditioning company's phone lights up at once. The one with a clear site and a working form catches the overflow.
openers.hook: Use this in late spring, before the first hot week. Name the season in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the first no-cool call: {demo-link}

openers.line: Furnaces quit on the coldest night, usually after dinner. When that call goes to voicemail, the family tries the next HVAC number until someone picks up.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it goes to a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A no-heat request that still works after dark: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring an HVAC tech. Good technicians look at whether a company looks organised before they leave a shop that already pays them.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note, a story or a sign on the van. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: An HVAC company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing says you service {City} and the towns around it, but nothing tells a homeowner in {Neighborhood} your vans come out there. Town plus 'furnace repair' is what they type.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A furnace and AC page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer monthly payments on a new furnace or air conditioner, that belongs on a page. A full system replacement is the number people want split up before they call.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing somewhere: a post, a review, the van wrap. If they don't, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: HVAC payment options explained before the visit: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your HVAC licence is on the state lookup, but a homeowner never sees it. Showing the licence and insurance plainly is what separates you from the guy on a classifieds post.
openers.hook: Look them up on the state licence board. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and warranty on one HVAC page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your furnace and AC work comes from repeat customers and their neighbours. That holds until a new family moves in and searches for heating and cooling instead of asking.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'have used them for years' or 'my neighbour recommended'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where an HVAC referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a tidy install, clean line set and a level pad. Work like that should be the first thing a stranger sees, not three scrolls down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished install on their grid and name it exactly: furnace, heat pump or condenser, and the town if they tagged it.
openers.linkLine: That HVAC install, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a clean install, tidy line set and a level pad.

I searched for HVAC companies in {City} and found {Business Name} on social but no site with your hours, your maintenance plan and a way to request a furnace or AC visit. I put together a sample HVAC page to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my last message got buried under service calls. Here's the sample HVAC site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a no-heat and no-cool request that asks what the system is doing, a maintenance plan sign-up, and a repair-or-replace guide. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for heating and cooling companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss in the busy season. Short version: I built a sample HVAC site for {Business Name}, with a service request, a maintenance plan sign-up and your licence up front, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link to look at tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"I know HVAC owners get called by marketing agencies every week. This isn't ads or a lead contract, it's a site you own. The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many town and service pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than the margin on one system changeout."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday evening?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before the next heat wave."

objections.objection: Agencies call me every week. You're just another one.
objections.handler: "Fair, HVAC is the most pitched trade there is. The difference is I built your site first instead of asking for a meeting. No ad budget, no lead contract, and you own the domain either way."

objections.objection: I'm already on a lead platform for HVAC calls.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to three or four shops at once and you pay whether you win the job or not. Your own site sends the no-heat call to one company, yours, and it's still there when you stop paying the platform."

objections.objection: Most of my work is repeat customers.
objections.handler: "Then the maintenance plan page is for them. Repeat customers sign up for the spring and autumn checks online, and you stop chasing them by phone every season."

objections.objection: It's the busy season, I don't have time for this.
objections.handler: "That's when the site earns its keep, because it takes requests while you're in an attic. I need about an hour from you in total, and most of it can be texts."
"Good, that's cheaper than me. Happy to hand over the service request form and the maintenance plan page. If it stalls before winter, the offer stands."

objections.objection: People just want the cheapest system.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones comparing what's in the quote: sizing, ductwork, the warranty, who answers when it breaks. That's what makes your number make sense."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}, because it's a service form, a maintenance plan page and a few town pages. One new plan member a month covers it."

email.subject: HVAC site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for HVAC companies in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name}, service form and maintenance plan included. I'll text the link. Have a look between calls. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} HVAC demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, the first cold snap is a few weeks out and the no-heat calls are about to start. Thought of you.

The HVAC site is still here whenever you want it, same price as before. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to the margin on one system changeout, never to an hourly rate. HVAC owners think in installs and plan members.
Price the maintenance plan sign-up as its own line when it takes payment and books the first tune-up.
Quote heat pump, furnace, AC and duct pages separately; each answers a different search and a different season.
Only build the after-hours request path for shops that actually take no-heat calls at night.
Town pages scale with the service area; quote per town, and only where they have real installs.
Agency-saturated vertical: lead with the finished demo and a short scope, never a package of ads.

lineItems.description: Max when it handles several plan levels, monthly or yearly billing, and books the first tune-up on sign-up.
Max when the page has its own symptom list, a repair-or-replace note and installs of that equipment type.
Max with a symptom picker, system age, thermostat reading and routing to the on-call tech's phone.
Max when each town page gets its own installs, a local review and permit notes for that town.
Max with home size, current equipment age, upload of the data plate and a booking slot for the in-home visit.

lineItems.item: Heat pump and rebate placeholder page
lineItems.description: Max when it covers cold-climate heat pumps, dual-fuel and bracketed rebate fields the owner fills and keeps current.
Max when the service request, maintenance plan and repair-or-replace guide are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Maintenance plan renewal campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every plan member gets a reminder before their spring AC check and autumn furnace check, and lapsed members get a renewal nudge. The plan stops leaking members."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the maintenance plan page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each HVAC visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening the furnace is running again, the homeowner gets a text asking how the tech did. Those reviews are what the next no-heat searcher reads."

whatElseYouSell.name: Local Services Ads with the licence check
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "HVAC is licence-checked on those ads, so the badge does the trust work. I set it up, dispute the junk leads and keep it to furnace and AC repair, not duct cleaning tyre-kickers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once reviews are flowing and their licence and insurance documents are current.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for each install
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every new furnace, heat pump or condenser goes on your Google profile with the town in the caption, so the map shows this month's installs."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live and a new install is finished.

whatElseYouSell.name: Install photo day with the crew
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One day riding along on two HVAC changeouts gives you before-and-after equipment shots, the crew at work and a gallery that looks like your company, not a stock furnace."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they have two installs booked back to back.

whatElseYouSell.name: Van wrap and yard sign artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your vans park in a driveway for hours on every HVAC install. A clean wrap and a yard sign with the site on them make the whole street remember who fixed the air."
whatElseYouSell.when: Right after launch, or when they add a van.

whatElseYouSell.name: Pre-season tune-up mailer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before the first heat wave, every past customer gets a postcard offering an AC check, and before the first frost, a furnace check. It fills the slow weeks between seasons."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in early spring and late summer, mail two weeks later.

whatElseYouSell.name: Aging-system replacement campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Past repair customers with older furnaces and air conditioners get a plain letter about replacement options before the system dies in a cold snap."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, once they have a list of repair customers with equipment ages.

withoutAI.whoPays: The supply house or distributor branch
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your HVAC supply house sells to every heating and cooling contractor in the region. Introduce me and I'll build their contractor finder and counter-hours page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have real budgets, and their contractor list is the prospect list you would otherwise build by hand.

withoutAI.whoPays: The electrical contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who runs the disconnect and the circuit when you set a new condenser or heat pump? I'll build their site too, and your install page links to theirs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: HVAC and electrical work the same installs and already refer each other. One introduction is a warm door.

withoutAI.whoPays: The insulation contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your tech finds a bare attic over the furnace, someone blows in insulation after. That crew needs a site, and your sizing page links to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Insulation is the natural next job after a load calculation. Both sides gain a referral partner.

withoutAI.route: Property managers with rental HVAC calls
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The managers whose rental furnaces you fix need a tenant maintenance request page. I build it, and the no-heat tickets route to your HVAC team."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers with dozens of doors have a real maintenance problem and an HVAC vendor they already trust.

withoutAI.route: Home inspectors who flag old furnaces
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every inspection report that flags an aging furnace or condenser sends a buyer looking for an HVAC company. The inspectors you know need sites as much as you did."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors and HVAC shops swap referrals at every sale. The inspector buys a site on the same logic: look established, get booked.

withoutAI.route: Duct cleaning and dryer vent operators
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The duct cleaner you send work to has the same problem you had: no site, all word of mouth. Your air quality page links to them and theirs back to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small duct cleaning firms sit next to HVAC in the homeowner's mind, and they rarely have anyone building for them.

withAI.route: Parts lookup assistant for the supply house
withAI.pitchLine: "Give every HVAC contractor on the branch's books a tool that turns a data plate photo into the right capacitor, motor or board, with branch stock and price."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties contractors to one branch's counter, which is worth more to the distributor than a rebate.

withAI.route: No-heat ticket triage for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants text 'the heat's off' at midnight. An assistant asks about the thermostat, the breaker and the filter, marks real outages urgent and sends them to one HVAC company."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers save dispatch time, and the HVAC client gets steady repair work from accounts that pay on time.

withAI.route: Plain-language report summaries for home inspectors
withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers don't read a long inspection report. An assistant turns it into a one-page summary with furnace, AC and water heater findings first."
withAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors compete on how clear their reports are, and the HVAC owner's introduction makes the first demo easy.

withAI.route: Quote follow-up for the electrician partner
withAI.pitchLine: "The electrician who wires your condensers loses panel quotes to slow callbacks. The same follow-up texts your HVAC office runs, set up for them in a week."
withAI.whyItWorks: You built it once for the HVAC client, so the second build is configuration, and the referral came from someone they trust.

withAI.pitchLine: "Energy raters who test homes before an HVAC replacement write long reports. An assistant drafts the homeowner summary, duct leakage and insulation first."
withAI.whyItWorks: Raters work alongside HVAC replacements constantly and have no time for writing. The HVAC owner already knows the good ones.

withAI.route: Comfort complaint log for small commercial landlords
withAI.pitchLine: "Strip-mall tenants complain the unit is too hot or too cold. An assistant logs each complaint by rooftop unit and spots the ones that need an HVAC visit, not a thermostat lecture."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small landlords juggle rooftop units and angry tenants with no system. The HVAC client gets the service calls.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for no-heat calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every call you miss in an attic gets a text asking for the address and whether the furnace or AC is fully down. You call back knowing which one can't wait."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Maintenance plan member manager
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every plan member, their equipment, their last tune-up and their renewal date in one list, with the spring AC checks and autumn furnace checks scheduled from it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their current member list, plan levels and the tune-up checklist.

softwareAI.name: System replacement price estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks the home size, gas or heat pump and efficiency level and sees a ballpark range for a new HVAC system before the in-home visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real price bands by system type and size, and the smallest job they take.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that name the HVAC repair
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted in your voice that mentions the furnace or AC fix and the tech, ready to approve from the van."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Needs ten of their past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tune-up reminder and booking texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before each season, every past HVAC customer gets a text with three open tune-up slots. They tap one, and it's on the board."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the customer list with last service dates and their calendar.

softwareAI.name: After-hours HVAC answering line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at midnight in a cold snap, walks the caller through the thermostat and breaker checks, books the visit and wakes the on-call tech only when it's a real no-heat."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, ahead of heating season. Needs their on-call rota, after-hours fee wording and the checks they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tech checklist app with startup readings
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Techs log pressures, temperature split and filter size on a phone at each tune-up, and the homeowner gets a clean HVAC report before the van leaves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their tune-up checklist, the readings they record and a tech willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Data plate reader for equipment age
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads the sticker off the furnace or condenser and the tool reads the model and likely age, so the office knows what's in the basement before the call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a sample of past data plates and their equipment notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; the tech always confirms on site.

softwareAI.name: Good-better-best HVAC proposal builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "At the kitchen table, the comfort adviser builds three HVAC system options with prices and monthly payments, and the homeowner signs on the tablet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their equipment tiers, pricing rules and the proposal they use on paper today.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote notes from the in-home visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house, talk about the ducts, the return and the attic, and it drafts the HVAC replacement quote on your template."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Filter delivery subscription for plan members
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every plan member gets the right-size furnace filter on their doorstep each season, billed automatically, with your sticker on the box."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs filter sizes from the member list and a supply source they already buy from.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on HVAC symptoms and plan questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'why is my air conditioning blowing warm' and 'what does the plan cover' at night from your own notes, and takes a number when it doesn't know."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their symptom notes, plan terms and service area, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Dispatch board for HVAC calls and installs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every repair call, tune-up and changeout on one board by tech and van, so the office stops juggling a whiteboard and three phones in a heat wave."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, when they run three or more vans. Needs their call types, techs and how they assign work today.

softwareAI.name: Repair-history lookup by address
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Type the address and see every furnace and AC visit, part and reading at that house, so the tech walks in knowing the history."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past invoices or service notes they can export.

softwareAI.name: Replacement-candidate finder from repair notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads a season of HVAC repair notes and flags homes with old equipment and repeat breakdowns, so the replacement letter goes to the right people."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of service notes with equipment ages. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Heat-wave and cold-snap alert to plan members
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a heat wave or hard freeze is forecast for {City}, plan members get a text with two quick HVAC checks and a priority booking link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the member list and a weather feed for their service area.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by install and van
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which HVAC installs actually made money once equipment, line sets, permits, callbacks and crew hours are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs equipment invoices and crew hours for a season of installs.

softwareAI.name: Callback and warranty claim tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every warranty part, callback and labour claim on HVAC equipment tracked until it's paid, so the shop stops eating parts it should be reimbursed for."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their open warranty claims and how they file them now.

softwareAI.name: Tech ride-along training notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Senior techs talk through a tricky heat pump or furnace fix on a phone, and it becomes a searchable how-to for the apprentices."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, once they hire apprentices. Needs a senior tech willing to record. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for HVAC techs and apprentices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants answer your questions about refrigerant handling, a clean driving record and on-call weekends, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and the pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the maintenance plan manager for HVAC shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built this maintenance plan manager for one HVAC shop. Every heating and cooling company with a plan runs it off a spreadsheet."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The hard part of vertical software is knowing the workflow. The first HVAC client taught it to you and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor finder licensed to an HVAC distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-a-contractor map on your site for every HVAC dealer who buys from your branches. They stay loyal to the branch that sends them installs."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on dealer loyalty, and a tool contractors use daily is stickier than a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer site program for an equipment maker's territory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your independent HVAC dealers need sites with a service request and plan sign-up. I've built that workflow for one already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers have co-op budgets and a dealer presence problem. The HVAC client is your proof you know the trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member HVAC contractor a site template with a licence display and maintenance plan page as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew, and licence visibility against unlicensed installers is already on their agenda.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: HVAC site template for marketing agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency signs heating and cooling shops and builds each from scratch. License my HVAC template with the no-heat request and plan sign-up already done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the HVAC relationship; you sell them the part you've already finished.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The trade school or community college programme
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The HVAC programme your client hires from needs a page that sells the course to school leavers and lists the shops that hire graduates."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools need enrolments and placements; the HVAC owner who hires their graduates is the warm introduction.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your participating HVAC contractors need one clear page each explaining the program. I've built the contractor side already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Efficiency programs have outreach budgets and struggle to get contractors to explain them well.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home warranty company's HVAC vendor network
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The home warranty company's regional office
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your HVAC vendors take your dispatch calls with no way to show customers who they are. A vendor page kit fixes that across the network."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Warranty firms live on vendor reliability, and a common page kit makes their network look professional.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Seasonal HVAC campaign kit for shops in other metros
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: HVAC companies outside your metro, monthly
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A switch-on heat-wave banner, cold-snap text and pre-season tune-up mailer, ready for any HVAC shop the week the weather turns."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every heating and cooling company needs the same campaign twice a year. A kit means no custom build each time.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each heating and cooling territory needs its own towns, on-call number and plan sign-up routed to the right owner. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many territories on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One HVAC shop per metro, next city over
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: An HVAC company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one heating and cooling company per city. {City} is spoken for; the next metro's best independent HVAC shop isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive geography matters in a saturated vertical, and the template, pitch and demo carry straight over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Commercial rooftop-unit service pages for mechanical contractors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Commercial HVAC contractors who service rooftop units for restaurants and offices need a capability page and a service agreement request, not a homeowner site."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Residential HVAC owners know the commercial shops in town, and those buyers pay more for a sharper site.

upsellLadder.offer: HVAC site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The HVAC site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new plan price or on-call number is a text to me, not a weekend for you."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests after each HVAC visit
upsellLadder.trigger: The first furnace or AC repair since launch, with a relieved homeowner.
upsellLadder.line: "That family whose furnace you fixed Tuesday is the review the next cold house reads. Let's ask every HVAC customer the same evening."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first members sign up through the maintenance plan page.
upsellLadder.line: "Plan members are signing up online now. Let's make sure every one of them renews before their next furnace check."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention tracking plan members in a spreadsheet or missing a tune-up.
upsellLadder.line: "Your plan members have outgrown the spreadsheet. This schedules every spring and autumn HVAC check for you."

upsellLadder.trigger: The missed-call log shows no-heat or no-cool calls after hours during a weather swing.
upsellLadder.line: "Those no-heat calls last cold night went to whoever answered first. This answers them and wakes the on-call tech only when it's real."

upsellLadder.offer: Local Services Ads with the licence check
upsellLadder.trigger: A steady count of new reviews and current licence and insurance documents.
upsellLadder.line: "Your reviews are strong enough now for the licence-checked HVAC ads. Let's put the badge in front of the next heat wave's searches."

upsellLadder.offer: Dispatch board for HVAC calls and installs
upsellLadder.trigger: They add a third van or mention the office drowning in calls during a heat wave.
upsellLadder.line: "Three HVAC vans and a ringing office won't fit on a whiteboard. Let's put every call and changeout on one board."

upsellLadder.trigger: A full year of repair notes on file and a slow shoulder season ahead.
upsellLadder.line: "A year of HVAC repair notes says which old systems are about to fail. Let's write to those homes before the cold does."
